text:
maria: Quick sync — proposing we start a Karpenter migration for GPU workloads in us-west-2. Main concerns: warm/prewarmed capacity, spot -> ondemand fallback, and IP/ENI pressure in high-concurrency launches. Can we sketch a canary plan + cost signal?

ashok: We ran a short Karpenter run in staging last week. Cold-start tail dropped ~40%, good. Observed a burst of ENI allocations when ~30 pods scheduled at once — caused transient pod pending. We should limit concurrent node launches and prefer smaller instance sizes to spread ENIs.

ashok: Example provisioner snippet I'm thinking of:
```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: gpu-canary
spec:
  requirements:
    - key: "node.kubernetes.io/instance-type"
      operator: In
      values: [g5.xlarge, g4dn.xlarge]
  provider:
    subnetSelector: {kubernetes.io/cluster/our-cluster: "owned"}
  limits:
    resources:
      cpu: "2000"
      nvidia.com/gpu: "50"
  ttlSecondsUntilExpired: 300
```

dena: Re: ENI/IP exhaustion — staging hit per-subnet IP limits with 100 g4dn.xlarge because each had many secondary IPs. Two mitigations: enable ENI trunking + consolidate into smaller instance families, or spread across AZs and add more subnets. Also add `ttlSecondsBeforeEviction` so short lived pods don't cause churn.

kevin: Cost angle: prewarmed nodes (warm pool) will raise baseline cost. But tail-latency reduction might be worth it. I can run a 7-day trace simulation with current request distribution if someone drops the trace (sample) into s3. We should measure cost-per-successful-inference and p99 latency delta.

maria: Suggested canary: route 3% of traffic to a Karpenter-backed nodepool in us-west-2a for 72 hours. Metrics to watch: pod pending > 30s, ENI allocations, node launch latency, % of launches falling back to ondemand, cost delta. Schedule drain window 02:00 PT if we need to rollback.

ashok: I'll create the canary provisioner and a small prewarm pool (5 nodes) with spot + `fallbackToOndemand: true`. Also enable burstLimiter to cap concurrent launches to 6.

ashok: Another config note — set `consolidation: disabled` for the canary so we don't evict during experiment.

dena: Add a watchdog: if > 5 pods pending for 120s in the canary namespace, trigger autoscaling group fallback and notify #incidents. Also enable metric alert for SubnetAvailableIpCount < 50%.

ops: Rollback playbook: annotate Deployments with `redwood.infra/node-pool: ca` to force CA-backed nodes, then scale down Karpenter provisioner to 0 and remove canary route. Documented in playbooks/runbook-karpenter-migration.md (internal).

infra-bot: [automated] canary-provisioner created in staging at 2024-11-08T14:12:30Z

deploy-bot: [info] will schedule prod canary at 2024-11-11T02:00:00Z if the simulation results are green.

kevin: I'll run the cost sim today and post results to the thread. If cost delta < 15% with p99 improvement >= 25%, +1 from me.

maria: Perfect — timeline: ashok to create provisioner + prewarm, kevin runs sim, dena sets ENI/watchdog alerts, ops readies rollback steps. Check back by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
